Priya (CSM): Hey team — Go-live for Meridian Health is next Wed. Customer is asking for a concise SLO acceptance package: uptime, p95 latency, and how credits would be calculated if we miss targets. Can ops + eng help draft?
Jordan (Eng): Happy to. Do we have an agreed SLO numbers in the contract?
Priya (CSM): Contract mentions 99.5% availability and p95 latency < 300ms for inference requests. There is an SLA credit clause but not a worked example.
Liam (SRE): Got it. I'll pull the last 30d signals and a baseline. Can we align on what counts as downtime? (region failures vs degraded latency)
Priya (CSM): Good Q — customer wants "service unavailability" as availability drops below target for >= 5m sustained per their legal team. For latency, they want p95 computed per calendar day per route.
Sam (Enablement): I can put together the one-pager that we send to customers. Will include example calculations + a short FAQ. Any docs style preferences?
Alex (Support): Add a short troubleshooting checklist for "warm start" vs cold-start latency spikes. They often ask that.
Jordan (Eng): For evidence, we should include: 1) raw query output for uptime (daily windows), 2) p95 latency histogram, 3) config showing routing and fallback model used. I can export JSON for (1) & (2).
Liam (SRE): ETA today: I'll run these queries and drop snapshots in the onboarding evidence folder. Query I plan to run: ```sql
-- uptime per day (simplified)
SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) as day,
  1 - (sum(downtime_ms)::float / (24*60*60*1000)) as availability
FROM infra.uptime_events
WHERE service = 'inference-router' AND customer_id = 'meridian'
  AND ts >= now() - interval '30 days'
GROUP BY day
ORDER BY day;
```
Jordan (Eng): For p95: ```json
{"route":"/v1/generate","period":"2024-01-01:2024-01-30","p95_ms":276}
``` I'll include per-region breakdown.
Priya (CSM): Perfect. Also need the sample credit calc in plain terms — legal wants a worked example for a 30-day billing period if availability is 99.2% (so below 99.5).
Sam (Enablement): I'll draft the worked example. Proposed wording: "If monthly availability < 99.5, customer receives X% credit proportional to minutes below target, capped at Y%." We'll need the exact cap from bizops.
Alex (Support): @ops-bot can you attach the KB link about latency warmup? :thumbsup:
ops-bot: KB link added: https://console.redwood.com/kb/latency-warmup (auto)
Liam (SRE): Quick note on measurement windows — we should match how billing calculates days (UTC rollovers). I'll annotate the export with timezone handling.
Jordan (Eng): Also we'll include screenshots of the Redwood Console SLO dashboard and the trace sample for a 95th percentile outlier.
Priya (CSM): Timeline: can we have a draft pack by EOD tomorrow? Customer briefing Thu afternoon.
Sam (Enablement): I can do the one-pager + FAQ by tomorrow noon.
Liam (SRE): I'll drop raw CSVs and the SQL into the folder by EOD today.
Jordan (Eng): I'll produce the p95 JSON and a short note on fallback model behavior by tomorrow morning.
Priya (CSM): Thanks — last ask: capture a short blurb about renewal risk if they perceive monitoring or credit calc as opaque. We should offer a 30m walkthrough during the briefing.
Alex (Support): I'll volunteer to run the walkthrough and take notes for an action list.
Sam (Enablement): I'll draft slides for the 30m walkthrough (2 slides on uptime, 2 on latency, 1 on credits, 1 on runbook).
Priya (CSM): Awesome. Follow-ups: @Liam please flag any anomalies > 0.2% deviation from baseline in the last 30d so we can preempt questions. @Jordan please add a short blurb on how automatic fallbacks affect latency measurement so we don't overcount transient spikes.
Liam (SRE): Will do. Found an early signal: 2024-01-12 had a 0.4% availability dip in us-west for ~12m. I'll include a short RCA note. :eyes:
Jordan (Eng): Noted — I'll explain fallback routing: when primary model pool is saturated we route to the cheaper replica which may add ~40ms tail. We'll document it as expected behavior.
Priya (CSM): Great — once everything is in the folder I will assemble and send the customer-facing package. Thanks team! :rocket:
